utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, all. For the Prosecution, I'm Tom Hannis along with Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, Ms. Tatjana Savic, and we are joined today by our intern, Ms. Margaret Artz. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the witness is escorted back into court, the Chamber is in receipt of a motion for reconsideration filed by the Prosecution, and we would request the Defence to make an expedited response -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we file our response by Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Monday. We think Monday would not be unreasonable. We would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. So would the usher please escort the witness back to the stand, if there are no other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just an information considering the scheduling. I've noticed yesterday at the end of the day that, in my opinion, the witness was experiencing some difficulty, tired. And, in my opinion, he was in pain again. So I decided to shorten direct examination of the witness, and perhaps I will use another three hours. So far, I spent only nine, and I guess I will -- I will use another, perhaps, three hours, maybe not even that, and I will finish in the course of today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. Much appreciated. In that vain, I suppose that what we should be thinking in terms of, should you complete within three hours, is an early adjournment today so the witness would have an opportunity to rest, and then Mr. Krgovic would begin his cross-examination when we resume on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think that would be the best solution, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We thank counsel for their consideration in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, good morning to you. Before Mr. Zecevic resumes, I remind you, you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Macar. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, in the late part of the yesterday's session, we talked about the action that took place in Zvornik to crush the Yellow Wasps. Were there similar problems elsewhere involving paramilitary groups throughout the RS of BiH in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were similar problems elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know whether there were problems involving paramilitary groups and organisations in Foca, for example?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document is 114, tab 54. 114D1, to be more specific. Sir, this is a memo by the Trebinje CSB signed as authorised by the chief, Krsto Savic, by someone apparently named Milorad Cuk. The date is the 3rd of August, 1992. It reads: "Given the increasing complex security situation in Foca municipality and the alleged attack on the police station carried out on 23rd of July, 1992, by military personnel from the so-called Dragan Nikolic Detachment of which we have already informed you, we hereby request that you urgently dispatch a special police detachment to intervene in the Foca area, and disband and disarm the paramilitary formations." Sir are you familiar with this particular incident, or were you familiar with it at the time, the 23rd of July incident, and the attack by that group on the Foca public security station?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about the Ministry of the Interior of the RS of BiH? What did they do about it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about this document, too. It was on the 3rd of August, 1992, that I came to Bijeljina where members of the special unit of the RS MUP were completing their activities, in relation to bringing in the Yellow Wasps back to Bijeljina from Zvornik municipality. That day, Mr. Cedo Kljajic met with me to discuss what to do with the Yellow Wasps, and we agreed that we had to urgently prepare to dispatch a special unit to the Foca area because of all these incidents that were occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to see this document at the time? Did Mr. Cedo Kljajic, as chief of the public security station, perhaps familiarise you with the substance of this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told about the substance of the document by Mr. Cedo Kljajic. Yes, that's true. I'm not sure if I saw the actual document, but he even went on to explain the broader context of everything that was going on in the Foca municipality at the time. I particularly wanted to know whether at least a portion of the unit would remain in the Bijeljina territory so that we could complete this operation of bringing in the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 115D1, tab 51 [as interpreted], dated the 4th of August. This is a cover letter accompanying a report by the Foca public security station regarding the 23rd of July incident, and also a petition by some citizens from Foca municipality who were beaten, mistreated, humiliated by this paramilitary group described here as the Dragan Nikolic Detachment. This was addressed to the police administration --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see in the transcript it is referred to as tab 51, but my tab 51 is something concerning the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I said 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is 115D1, tab 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with the report. Nevertheless, I learned from Mr. Cedo Kljajic about it. We spent those days discussing the possibility of dislocating or dispatching the special police unit. I wanted to get this done because of the Yellow Wasps, specifically. I learned about the extent of the problem in Foca municipality on those days from Mr. Cedo Kljajic, but I did not, myself, have a chance to see the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, given what the witness just stated, I would move that the previous document, 114D1, tab 54, be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like a clarification when introducing the document. Mr. Zecevic, at page 3, line 19, stated that it appeared to have been signed by a particular named person. The writing looks too long to be that name, and the witness didn't indicate what the name was. So could we have some clarification about that, if the witness can provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let's go back to 114D1, tab 54. Sir, first of all, the handwritten part, the signature, and the abbreviation where it says "authorised by," is that the Latin script or the Cyrillic script?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the Cyrillic script.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to read the name of the person who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the police section in the Trebinje public security station, Mr. Sokolic Murat [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Milorad Cuk?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milorad Cuk. We see the name Sokolic Murat emerging on the LiveNote but it is probably going to be changed later on. Do you perhaps know what position Mr. Milorad Cuk held at the time in the Trebinje public security station?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was head of the uniformed police department in the Trebinje CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Hannis, if that satisfies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If he says that's what the name says, then I'm satisfied. And it appears to me it's the same signature on 115D1 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Your application is for the admission of 114? And the -- as I understood your application was premised on what the witness said about 115. Am I missing something? I see the basis of the application, 114. That stands on its own. But what is the connection between this and 115?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I just wanted -- because basically both the document refer to the same incident on the 23rd of July in Foca, and I just wanted to find out whether the witness was aware of this second document or the actual report filed by the SJB Foca. Now my next document is in connection with 115D1, and I don't think that we need to introduce two documents on the -- on precisely the same subject. And the document 114D1, tab 54, the witness confirmed that he was discussing the contents of that document with Mr. Cedo Kljajic and was aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I find myself in an unusual position, Your Honour. If you're going to admit one, I'd ask that you admit both. They're clearly connected, and, for my purposes, they show communications occurring smoothly and regularly and timely because it occurs the very next day. And it's going from Trebinje to Sarajevo and apparently being seen in Bijeljina as well. So I would like to have them both in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And where are we in terms of the report to which 115 is the cover?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't have that report, Your Honours, unfortunately. We just have this cover -- cover letter which was sent together with the report, but the report was never found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. So both documents are admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, as Exhibits 1D647 and 1D648, respectively. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the next document is 23D1, tab 56. This is a report by Vojin Vukovic and Cedo Tosic, both police inspectors, dated the 10th of August, 1992. Report on the repeated monitoring of the implementation of the Serbian Republic of BH interior minister's order, strictly confidential number 10-17 of the 27th of July, 1992. Two signatures there, I assume those to belong to the two inspectors mentioned in the document. Are you familiar with these two gentlemen, Tosic and Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know them as uniformed police officers working at the ministry's HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, at page 3 of this document, which I assumed to be page 2 of the English. My apologies. It should be the bottom of page 1 of the English text. It reads: "Having carried out an inspection, they propose certain measures and steps to be taken." The Serbian page is all right. Page 2 in the English version, please. Can we bring that back. It goes on to state: "In the area of the Foca SJB, send a special unit or a part of the unit of the MUP of the Serbian Republic of BH as soon as possible. The objective being to destroy outlaw groups and paramilitary formation and establish and strengthen the human resources at the SJB which must then assume the responsibility of securing the conditions for the normal functioning of civilian authorities." Number 2: "Replace the supervisors at the Gacko SJB in order to normalise the current situation and regain the trust of citizens in the MUP organs. Urgently prosecute crime perpetrators and hold them to account." Sir, the inspectors here comment on the situation at the Foca SJB and the situation at the Gacko SJB. As for Foca, we've seen that already, and we know that you knew about this at the time. What about the situation in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a briefing held in August in Mr. Cedo Kljajic's office. At this briefing, he told me about the fact that the problems in Gacko were escalating because the supervisors realised that there was more and more disruption of public order in Gacko. And it was quite clear that the people in charge of the public security station were unable to restore peace and stability to the area. I think proposals were made at that briefing to dispatch special police units of the Ministry of the Interior to the area in order to help the public security station bring the situation back to normal and pick new supervisors for that police station.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness apologised for speaking too fast. It was not recorded, probably because the interpreters did not hear it because I was asking my question at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, do you know whether at the Gacko SJB there was a replacement?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. There was a replacement carried out at the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When we say a replacement, was this a replacement of the executive staff, of the leaders of the public security station, and can you more or less remember the actual date when this took place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was late in August or early in September. I cannot be sure at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, sir, whether this special unit, at the end of August of 1992, did, indeed, leave and go to Foca?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, I think it did not go to Foca because of the specific situation with communications towards Foca. I know that it had to report to the ministries of the interior of Serbia and Montenegro. Any passages of armed units had to be reported to them. And as far as I can remember, because of such and similar problems, I believe that that did not take place. I cannot be sure, but I don't think that they went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there no objections, I should like to move this document to be admitted into the case file as it is associated with the previous two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D649, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown document 963D1, which is tab 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a letter. It was type written and signed for the minister of the interior, Mico Stanisic, by someone else. It is dated the 28th of November, 1992. And it is addressed to the ministries of the interior of the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Montenegro. And it reads: "In order to protect the security of the property of citizens in the territory of eastern Herzegovina, Republika Srpska, we must move a part of the special unit and the necessary equipment from Zvornik across the territories of Serbia and Montenegro. The movements would take place on the 29th of November, 1992, at 2000 hours from Zvornik. Since this is the only route available to us, we ask that you allow free passage of the unit so that it can carry out its planned task." And then it goes on to say, to indicate the actual route that would be followed by the unit in question, that is, via Bajina Basta, Zlatibor, Prijepolje, so a part of Serbian and a part of Montenegrin territory. Sir, are aware of the fact -- in fact, please first tell me what municipalities does eastern Herzegovina encompass, and to which CSB do those municipalities belong, in territorial terms?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, I believe that there were 12 municipalities -- I apologise, yes. I believe that there were 12 municipalities that were compromised within the territory of Herzegovina and, in organisational terms, within the Ministry of the Interior security affairs within the remit of the Trebinje centre for public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was Gacko municipality and that of Trebinje and Bilice, are these municipalities in eastern Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the area of eastern Herzegovina. Trebinje, Bilice, Gacko, Nevesinje, Glogine [phoen], even a part of Mostar municipality which was under Serbian control, then also Foca, a part of Gorazde, Cajnice, Rudo, Visegrad municipalities. Perhaps I have omitted some.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And what about Visegrad? Was it also a part of that territory?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Visegrad was a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this special unit or a part of that special unit was, indeed, given permission at the end of November by the MUPs of Serbia and Montenegro to pass through that territory and went to the territory of eastern Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I should like to remark that this document was produced by Cvijetin Lekic, an inspector from the police administration, and he signed it also. This was standard procedure to announce to the ministries of the adjacent republics any such moves. And as far as I can recall, members of the special police detachment which was in Zvornik were in the territory of Gacko municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that in this particular instance, in contrast to the Foca case, the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia and that of -- and of Montenegro actually gave its permission for the special unit to pass through its territory?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without permission, any uniformed police with or without armaments would not be able to pass; and in particular, not if they were armed and had hardware. Without announcing their route and obtaining such permission, they would not have been able to pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly that -- that you answered -- that your answer to my question was affirmative?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I should like to move that this document be admitted into the case file.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I take it from the witness's answer that the signature is the signature of the person named at the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That was my understanding as well, because he said he was the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that case, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D650, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to show you the next document, 1D334, MFI; the tab number is 80. Sir, this is a document dated the 25th of October, 1992, of the public security station of Visegrad, addressed to the Bijeljina MUP, the crime prevention administration, and to the competent Trebinje CSB, signed by chief Risto Perisic. It has to do with operations in a particular case. Please tell me, firstly, when were communications, either system of dispatching dispatches in the territory of Republika Srpska, when did that start to function in a normal way in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The system of sending dispatches with the relocation to Bijeljina and the creation of technical preconditions was significantly improved sometime from mid-October, although there still remained some problems, but the system kept being improved in the field as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, who was the chief of the Visegrad public security station in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the chief of the station was Mr. Perisic, but I had no occasion to meet him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document refers to a case of the kidnapping of 18 Muslims under Rudo-Priboj road in the territory of the Visegrad public security station. Are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that case. I believe that we were informed by the MUP of Serbia about this incident, as far as I can recall, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, what was this incident about, this kidnapping? What was it about; and how come you were informed about it by the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a border area between Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. The road, actually, crosses from Serbia to Bosnia, and I believe that this is an railway line also in that area. To the best of my recollection, we were informed that the relatives of the kidnapped had reported their disappearance. They had reported them from missing from Priboj, I believe, to the effect that a group of armed people in military uniforms had taken a group of citizens off a bus, and I believe that this was reported to the MUP of Serbia. And we were informed on that basis and on our part, asked the station, these police station to actually establish the fact. We sent them a request to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we have not been able to locate that particular document. We do not have it. Tell me, this route that you -- is referred to, Rudo to Priboj, that particular road, I believe that you explained, but it is not quite clear. Just please confirm whether I understood you correctly. So this route goes from Serbia, from the territory of Serbia, through the territory of Serbia, and then partly goes through the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then comes back to the territory of Serbia again. And both these towns, both these cities, are, in fact, in the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Rudo is in Bosnia and Herzegovina territory; and Priboj is in Serbian territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I shall show you the next document, and I believe it might refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 1D335, MFI, tab 81.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the following day, dated the 26th of October, which is a report regarding the kidnapping of 18 Muslim passengers which took place on the 22nd of October, 1992, in the place called Mioca, Rudo municipality. This document was signed by the chief of the Rudo public security station and the Visegrad public security station chief, Risto Perisic. Tell me, did you know Dragan Radjen, the chief of the Rudo station?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document and tell me if it jogs your memory about the incident itself, the kidnapping of these persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, due to overlapping speakers, the answer to your previous question wasn't recorded. The question was: "Tell me, did you know Dragan Radjen, the chief of the Rudo station?"

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see, Your Honours. I'm sorry, I was -- I had the document on my monitor so I didn't notice this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, again, we need to make a pause between my questions and your answers. The question was: Did you know Dragan Radjen, the chief of the Rudo public security station?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember his last name, but I did not know him personally. Never met him. If I may just answer your following question. I know about this situation. This definitely jogs my memory. The line overlaps across two municipalities. There were certain activities being pursued, in terms of shedding light on this report. There were two stations that took charge of this task: The Rudo station and the Visegrad station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, unless there are any objections, I would like the MFI to be taken off both these documents so they may be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure of the relevance of these. Rudo is not a municipality that's in our indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But Visegrad is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, as I understand it, this crime occurred in Rudo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The witness just confirmed that it occurred basically in Rudo and in Visegrad, on the territory of both municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, the document itself that we're looking at says: Information about the kidnapping of 17 passengers of Muslim ethnicity which happened on 22 October in the municipality of Rudo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this location, Mioca, in Rudo municipality, do you remember if that is the location of the kidnapping? Could you provide some detail on the incident, if you can?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that I can remember, Rudo and Visegrad are two adjacent municipalities crossed by the same road. It would be hard for me to draw the line separating the two municipalities now. Rudo is a small municipality with very few police officers working there, or was at the time. In the early stages, we didn't know exactly where the crime occurred. That is why the same instructions were received by both Rudo and Visegrad: Work in your own area and try to shed light on these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, were there any doubts surrounding the identity of the perpetrators? Or, rather, I don't mean doubts. I mean suspicions, in terms of intelligence suggesting who these persons might be.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were assumptions made by the Visegrad station, specifically. In all likelihood, they believed the crime had been perpetrated by members of paramilitary units from the neighbouring republics. At one point, a suspicion arose that the crime had been committed by members of the same ethnicity from Serbia and Montenegro, in order to cause an incident in the border area. Those were some assumptions being made initially when one first found out about the kidnapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was there any intelligence at any point that you received suggesting that Milan Lukic's group had been involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a later stage, we started suspecting that Milan Lukic's group was to blame for that incident. We received information at a later stage suggesting that Serbia's MUP had attempted to get more information on his activity and the activity of his units. At one point, Mr. Lukic was placed in custody. This was done at the time by the Uzice police administration or whatever form of organisation they were using at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic and his group, from which municipality were they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Mr. Lukic was from Bosnia and Herzegovina but was residing in Serbia before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know that Mr. Lukic and his group were operating, or were based in Visegrad municipality, and they were suspected of committing a number of crimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object to the leading nature of the question. Why doesn't he [Overlapping speakers] ... ask him where he was based, not isn't it true he was based in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my question was: Does the witness know. That's how I phrased my question. If he doesn't know, he might as well say that: No, I don't know. I do not believe that I was in any way at all leading the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It would be non-leading if it didn't contain the answer he is looking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I agree with Mr. Hannis, Mr. Zecevic. But I suppose you're still setting up the basis for the admissibility of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could you remind me as to why it was only marked for identification, not fully admitted as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, Your Honours, I see the time, and during the break I will find out and inform the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we will take the break now and resume in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, already the break, I checked the transcript. It's page 12735. Date is 29th of June, 2010. It was during the testimony of Witness -- the prosecutor from Visegrad. And the documents were offered by Mr. Cvijetic, and there was objection from the -- from the -- from the Office of the Prosecutor, and Your Honours' ruling was: "In the Chamber's view, the documents are admissible but not through this witness so they would be marked for identification."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. If we may have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In the Chamber's view, we have heard sufficient from this witness that the -- such as that the MFI qualification may now be lifted and marked as a full exhibit [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. It refers to documents 1D334 and 335. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 41D1, which is tab 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is an order by the minister of the interior. I'm unable to identify the signature, and you can try and give us a hand with that. The date is the 27th of October, 1992. The order was sent to the detachment of special MUP units, ordering that 50 police officers from the special MUP unit detachment and one of the managing staff be deployed on the territory of the Rudo and Visegrad SJBs in order to control roads, persons entering and leaving the territory of Republika Srpska, preventing crimes and other activities. It also says that the unit will be on its way on the 27th of October, 1992, at 1300 hours. Sir, this is the day after the previous report that we looked at, or, rather, the two reports dated the 25th and 26th of October, respectively. This is now the 27th of October, 1992. And this is an order. Have you seen this document before, sir, and do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this document. It was signed by Mr. Milos Zuban, chief of the police administration. The order was a result of an assessment that was made of the situation in Visegrad and Rudo municipalities, particularly because the border separating Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia proved to be very porous. There were several roads crossing the border, and at the time, we didn't have a proper border police set up or anything like that, nor, indeed, were we able to place the roads under control with the assistance of the local police. On the other hand, we suspected that there were paramilitary units active in the area, and there were incursions by criminal groups from Serbia itself. For these reasons, we decided to dispatch a number of the special police to the municipalities of Visegrad and Rudo to help out the local police with their work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We see a handwritten addition in the upper right corner, someone's initials, too. Could you identify those for us, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads: Sent to the unit A/A, whoever was in charge of dispatching this document. This is someone in the communication centre but the text reads sent to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know if the unit eventually left for the territory covered by the Rudo and Visegrad SJBs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, I think the unit was actually of two of those municipalities to help out the local police there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please just look again at the handwritten portion. Does it say "units sent"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, "units sent" in the Cyrillic script.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What's your understanding of what it says, "units sent"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was carried out to send units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Based on your recollection, what about the order and the fact that these 50 members of the MUP special units were dispatched there? Is that, among other things, also in reference to the kidnapping incident that we talked about a while ago, where 17 ethnic Muslims were kidnapped in those two municipalities?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember what the investigation yielded in the case of these 17 Muslims being kidnapped? What was the outcome; and were those persons ever found?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the persons were found. The Visegrad and Rudo SJBs and the Sarajevo CSB did not manage to obtain any intelligence regarding the identity of the perpetrators. I'm talking about the incident involving the kidnapping of these 17 Muslims, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objection, I would like to tender this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D651, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, before we move onto something else, I thought you said before the break that the suspicions were that it was Mr. Milan Lukic and his group who had conducted the kidnapping of those 18 Muslims in Rudo or Visegrad, or wherever it was. And I'm just curious to know, was that confirmed in the end? Did you find out in the end who had been responsible for the kidnapping; and were those people prosecuted for the events? What happened? What was the end of the story?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Visegrad and Rudo SJBs and the criminal police of the Sarajevo CSB, later on, because in terms of organisation it also belonged to the CSB Sarajevo, did not obtain any intelligence identifying the perpetrators of this crime. Therefore, no criminal report was filed because no evidence was obtained identifying the perpetrators. I'm not sure if that is specific enough for your purposes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's fine. And just one additional question: Do you know if the 18 Muslims were ever seen again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, not for as long as I worked with the police administration. I'm not sure what happened after the war. I'm not sure if their remains were ever found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Back to you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you perhaps know whether a criminal report was filed against unknown perpetrators, in relation to the kidnapping of these 17 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think he answered that question when he was speaking to Judge Harhoff. Page 23, line 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But that is precisely what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I answered Judge Harhoff, the perpetrators were not identified, and no criminal report materialised. It was the SJBs' responsibility to forward a report to the prosecutor regarding the fact that some persons went missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, what about the crime prevention administration? What about after this incident, the period of time that followed? Did it conduct an investigation into the kidnapping and disappearance of these ethnic Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime police administration continued to follow the kidnapping case. It tried to get through to the SJB in order to have more information on any reports of these missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 51D1, tab 83, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document produced by the crime prevention administration in Bijeljina. The number is 02-43, from 1993. Dated the 15th of March, 1993. It reads: "Report on the inspection of Trebinje Security Services Centre, Trebinje SJB, Visegrad SJB, Rudo, Cajnice, Gacko, and Nevesinje," signed by Nikola Milanovic, the person submitting the report. Sir, which organisational administration did Nikola Milanovic belong to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was inspector of the crime prevention police at the ministry's HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that your crime police administration of which you were head at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, paragraph 1 reads: "Nikola Milanovic, crime inspector with the crime prevention administration of the Republika Srpska MUP, and Dragan Obradovic, inspector with the administration for police duties and tasks ... on the 4th of March, 1993, arrived at the Visegrad SJB. Their task being to establish facts regarding the hijacking of passengers from aboard a Belgrade-Bar intercity train that had taken place there Stprci, Visegrad municipality. With regard to this case, a meeting was held at the Visegrad SJB attended by the head, the deputy commander," and so on and so forth, "as well as Milorad Cuk and Dragan Gagovic from the Trebinje CSB HQ. A special report was compiled about this event which was submitted to the Republika Srpska MUP officials." Sir, Mr. Nikola Milanovic here claims that he had a task. Who gave him this task, the task of establishing facts surrounding this kidnapping case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the procedure applied in the work of the Ministry of the Interior and specifically what the public security sector did, they often -- they often had these working meetings to discuss certain types of problems. It was at one of these meetings that the decision was taken to dispatch to Visegrad, in the Centar area, a mixed team comprising crime police administration inspectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the document speaks for itself. It's all there. The question was this: Who gave Nikola Milanovic this task? Who told him to ascertain facts surrounding the kidnapping of Muslims in Visegrad SJB, in an area covered by the Visegrad SJB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document says that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I need to interject. In my English translation I'm not sure I see a reference to hijacked persons being Muslims. Could counsel direct me to where there is such a reference? My English translation just says "persons" or "passengers."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is exactly what I'm trying to establish right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, the question shouldn't suggest that it says Muslims. That should come from the witness not from counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, sir, it is stated here that the passengers who were kidnapped in Strpci, Visegrad municipality -- does this kidnapping refer to the documents, the previous documents that we saw, or does it not? Is the case identical?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a instance of the kidnapping of passengers from a train on the Belgrade-Bar railroad in the part of territory which passes through Bosnia and Herzegovina, i.e., the village of Strpci which is a border village adjacent to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then please explain to us, shed more light on this incident for us, please, to the best of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior was informed that, on the route, on the railroad line from Belgrade to Bar in the area of the village of Strpci, a group of citizens have been taken off the train.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we go much farther, could we inquire about the date of this particular incident? It may bear on relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you assist us in this regard, Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in hindsight, from this distance, I can't be sure whether it was the second half of 1992, the end of 1992. It is hard for me to recall the exact date. But I do know that it is an incident that elicited greater tension in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please explain the facts that you are aware of in connection with this incident.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that a group of citizens were taken off the train in this area which immediately elicited reactions, actually, a demand forwarded to the Visegrad public security station to collect all relevant information. Then this was followed by an order to dispatch this mixed team. At a meeting in the Trebinje CSB, it was decided that all support should be given to the team in connection with this incident to see how they would conduct their operative actions in the field and possibly to establish the identity of the perpetrators of the -- that offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the persons who went missing, who were taken off the train, what was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons taken off the train were ethnic Muslims, I believe from the area of the municipality -- or, rather, the area at the border between Montenegro and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many persons were involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the exact number, and I would not wish to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were there 10, 20, more than 20?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly more than 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What was the intelligence that was gathered by the police in connection with the possible perpetrators of this crime?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information collected by the police was that these persons were taken away by a number of persons who were in military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any suspicions in respect of any specific individuals in this particular instance?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was suspicions, but it all literally boiled down to just suspicions. There was no tangible information that might be indicia, that a certain person committed that crime. I know that some attention was also focussed on Mr. Lukic at the time. But apart from speculations, there was nothing tangible, in terms of tangible material on the basis of which any further action could have been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These persons of Muslim ethnicity who were taken off the train, whose citizens were they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were citizens of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were these persons ever found?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any criminal proceedings were instituted in connection with the disappearance of these persons?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that criminal proceedings were conducted in Serbia against Mr. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the reason was for the criminal proceedings to have been conducted in the territory of the Republic of Serbia and not on the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in the period in question, Mr. Lukic was in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, and to the best of my recollection, he is a citizen of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objection, I move to tender this report as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have an objection as to relevance. The witness has indicated he doesn't remember the date of the event. He thinks it might be in the second half of 1992. The best we can say from this report is that it must have occurred before the 15th of March, 1993. And the fact that we have here is that an investigation was done in March of 1993 at a time when Mr. Stanisic, Mico Stanisic, was not the minister of the interior, so I'm not sure how that is relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I believe that it is relevant for a number of reasons. First of all, this is a document which was filed by an inspector who worked for the crime prevention administration that the witness was head of at that time as well as in 1992. The witness cannot state with certainty whether this incident took place in 1992 or at the beginning of 1993, but that notwithstanding, it was he who charged this inspector with the task of establishing the relevant facts, and he has explained in detail why he had done so and what was in question. On the first page of this document, in particular, there are references to the previous incident which took place in 1992 that we have already discussed, the hijacking of the bus passengers, so that it is in that sense associated with the other already admitted evidence and relevant on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I would point out in my English translation, page 2, talking about Rudo. And the second paragraph under Rudo SJB says: "In 1992, in the area of responsibility of Rudo, passengers from a bus had been taken in a place called Sjeverin." S-j-e-v-e-r-i-n. The documents that we looked at before 1D334 and 335 made reference to passengers taken off a bus in Mioca, M-i-o-c-e. So it is not clear from looking at this document that it is talking about the same event. And again, my objection is, at best, this shows that this witness in 1993 directed somebody working for him to do an investigation. What has that got to do with Mico Stanisic and his responsibility in 1992? Nothing, I say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if the -- if the -- if the position of the Office of the Prosecutor is that the JCE, alleged JCE, stopped after Mico Stanisic was removed from his position as a minister of the interior of Republika Srpska, we would like to be informed about that because, so far, we understood that -- that the allegation by the Office of the Prosecutor was that there was this overwhelming JCE starting from October 1991 and continuing until end of 1995. But I appreciate Mr. Hannis's comment about the second incident, and I will inquire with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Macar, on the first page here, the penultimate paragraph, it is stated: "In the area of the Rudo SJB, 1992, passengers were kidnapped from a bus in the village of Sjeverin. And it was advised that this case should be processed because there is intelligence on the perpetrators of the persons who were -- would be kidnapped and the case should be worked on until the final position on the case is taken." There's now a reference to Sjeverin. We have reference to Sjeverin in this part. And previously, we saw that in the previous documents there was information about the village of Mioca, in the municipality of Rudo. Could you be of assistance and tell us whether these were two distinction incidents and what is in question?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same incident.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Will the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, Mr. Macar, you heard the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We must pause between question and answer, please. Please be so kind as to explain to us then why the previous documents refer to the village of Mioca and this document to a placed named Sjeverin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably it was based on the initial information gathered and because of the need to speedily relay the information. That might account for the mistake. But this -- this place, this incident, this hijacking took place there Sjeverin and that it was reported as such, as persons going missing. When the team was dispatched to inspect the field, one of their tasks was to check the quality of the gathered information and to actually confirm it so that it could be the basis for further work and to establish whether the task required the inclusion of additional forces. Generally, they were to assist the current stage of the task on the day of their inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So let us clarify. The kidnapping of the passengers from the bus, information about which was dispatched in October 1992 from the Rudo public security station and the one in Visegrad regarding the kidnapping that took place in the village of Mioca, this other incident which is described here as the kidnapping of passengers in Sjeverin, if I understood you properly, you say that this is the same incident?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason why the designated place of the commission of this act was changed in the period from October 1992 until early 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the collected information, because in rural areas --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please concentrate on my question. Please answer my question and then we shall go onto remark on the rural area and similar.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instructions given to Mr. Milanovic to check the information was issued to him according to the instruction that we got from the Visegrad station in 1992, in respect of the missing persons from the bus, as I described a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, do you allow for the possibility that the actual place of the commission of the crime, the designation of the actual place of the commission of crime, was the result of the investigation of this offence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was what I was trying to say when you interrupted me. Yes, that was exactly the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that, ultimately -- do you remember whether it was at all indisputably established in this case where the kidnapping of the passengers had taken place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the approximately correct location was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which was -- which is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, in hindsight, it is Sjeverin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I move to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, I wanted to indicate that the indictment, to the best of my recollection, alleged that the JCE from October 1991 to the end of December 1992, not 1995. And so I maintain my objection about the relevance of this investigation in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But it does touch and concern matters which, according to the witness, I don't want to put words in his mouth, probably but could have occurred in 1992, which was -- a part of your initial objection, Mr. Hannis. Isn't that sufficient for our purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I guess if you only focus on the event concerning passengers taken off a bus in Rudo in 1992 and not passengers taken off the Belgrade-Bar bus sometime before March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a not a Belgrade-Bar bus. It's a Belgrade-Bar train.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the witness could not specify whether it happened at the end of 1992, the second part of 1992, or possibly in beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But my point regarding the train is that there was no investigation, apparently, ordered about that before March of 1993 when Mr. Stanisic was no longer the minister and had not yet become minister again for a second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the document is admitted and marked. It goes without saying that when the time comes to assess the document, such of it as is irrelevant, will clearly fall away.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Exhibit 1D652.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P163, tab 59.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a summary from the working group meeting of the senior staff members of the minister of the interior, the meeting held on the 20th of August, 1992, in Trebinje. Are you familiar with this document; and did you attend this meeting in Trebinje on the 20th of August?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on page 13 -- or, rather, page 14 of this document in Serbian, in e-court, we see a paragraph starting with the following words: "Macar, Goran." And then it goes on to convey what you apparently said at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 17 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this part. And I remember these words of mine, where I pointed out to the fact that the crime services need to intensify their work. But, additionally, I also informed them about the problem whereby the crime investigation workers, without the uniformed policemen and other staff members, could not deal with the cases where there were armed groups of criminals involved, that other methods and other approaches were needed to deal with that. I gave an example of Foca, and there were other examples, too. I remember a collegium meeting we had because of an incident that had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What incident was it about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to repeat that one had to travel to Trebinje via Serbia and Montenegro. We set out in civilian clothes, and we were not armed. And the colleague who travelled with me took his police blue uniform. After the meeting concluded, in the building of the centre, since this was in the late afternoon hours, we were rushing to get ready to travel back to Bijeljina. My colleague was in his blue police uniform, and he wanted to change into civilian clothes just before the border with Montenegro. And as we left Trebinje, we were stopped by this big soldier. He waved to us and -- indicating that he wanted us to give him a ride somewhere. And as soon as he saw my colleague in a blue uniform, and this soldier had a machine-gun, 84 type, he started cursing police. He made us get out of the car and lie down on the road. I know that we did that under fierce threats coming from him, and we also noticed that there was another man in a similar position lying on the road. So we stayed there for ten or so minutes. And I think that somebody came by in a military truck, somebody wearing a uniform, and they managed to convince this soldier to let us go. It was quite a tense situation, this soldier with a big 84 machine-gun holding us there for some half an hour. This was just after we left Trebinje. And it was a good illustration of the situation as it was at the time. This was an individual incident. It did not -- it was not general position that the army had towards the police, but, unfortunately, I lived through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D348, which is tab 65.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Before we look at this document, tell me, please, in late August, did you participate in the work of some commission looking into the situation in the Bijeljina SJB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to his order -- to whose order this commission was set up; and do you remember who were its members?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission was set up pursuant to the order of the minister, Mr. Stanisic. It was a three-member commission: Gajic, Sreto; Spasojevic, Zoran; and me. I think that Spasojevic, Zoran worked at the SJB Bijeljina, and Sreto Gajic worked in the police administration in the ministry headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the reason and what was the task of this commission?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The task of the commission was to record the materiel and technical equipment at the Bijeljina SJB, to audit the deposits at the Bijeljina SJB, due to the information we received about the fact that some confiscated funds and items were unlawfully handled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we have this report before us. Would you please confirm whether this is your signature under number 1; and is this, indeed, the report that you wrote after inspecting the Bijeljina SJB and the situation there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the report signed by the members of the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Signature under number 1 is whose?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My signature is under number 1. Gajic is number 2. And Spasojevic is number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me briefly, what was the conclusion of the commission?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion of the commission was that it was established that the items deposited at the SJB were not handled in accordance with the law, and that pursuant to the order of Mr. Cedo Kljajic, some items were requisitioned. And later on, we heard that Mr. Andan, who used to work at the Ministry of the Interior, also took some items; whereas, some items were given to certain staff members of the station for their personal use. The funds, the money, was used to repair vehicles and for some operative expenses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did the commission reach the conclusion -- or, rather, what was the conclusion of the commission regarding the lawfulness of such a method of work, given the then-existing regulations?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established that these actions were contrary to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, perhaps before you move on, we can take the break now --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I'm sorry. I missed the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- and resume in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, as soon as the witness resumes the stand, the Chamber is minded to go into private session so that we, in the presence of the witness, can get an understanding of the rest of the day's scheduling, for obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before Mr. Zecevic continues his questions, there are some issues which the Chamber wishes to resolve, and I ask that we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, we talked about the findings of this commission. Do you know whether any disciplinary or any other types of measures were taken against any staff members of the Ministry of the Interior, as a result of the findings of the commission whose member you were?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that after the first findings of the commission, a disciplinary measure was meted out against Mr. Andan the very next month. And, further on, based on these findings, other checks were made concerning all items. Interviews were had with all of the persons who requisitioned any of the items, so all kinds of checks were made; following which, additional disciplinary measures were needed. I can't remember the exact situation, but I think that the further checks took an additional month because some of the persons that needed to be interviewed were not available. They were either on the front or busy with other assignments. So it took another month or two to complete further checks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what happened with the under-secretary for public security, Mr. Cedo Kljajic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr. Cedo Kljajic did not wait for the checks to be concluded. Disciplinary action needed to be taken against him, too. I don't know whether he received some advance notice or something. I just know that he was gone. For a period of time, he was gone. And based on what I learned, he had gone to Serbia. So not even the disciplinary commission of the Ministry of the Interior could take action against him, could institute proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You say that he went to Serbia. Did he terminate his employment with the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very fact that he left his job with the ministry means that he terminated his employment. He was also a military conscript who had wartime assignments pursuant to the enactments of the Ministry of the Interior, where he held a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Based on your information, did Mr. Kljajic come back to the Ministry of the Interior of the RS of Bosnia and Herzegovina, following his departure in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I have to ask you for a clarification based on the document of Mr. Hannis, which we can see on the transcript page 34, line 9 to 12. This is related to the documents that we tendered. Mr. Macar, tell me, please, what is the obligation of the organs of the interior upon learning that a crime was committed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- once they learned that a crime was committed, the organs are duty-bound, first, to establish what crime it was, where it was committed; then to carry out an on-site investigation; to fix all the traces on the site; to turn them all over to forensic department. Unfortunately, in 1992, such work could only be carried out partially by the Banja Luka CSB with their forensic department; whereas, other newly established centres, including the Doboj centre, were not able to carry out such forensic work. The forensic equipment of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina was located in Sarajevo in two different locations. And most of the experts who used to work in those services were top experts in their field, but were ethnic Muslims. And it wasn't until early 1993, owing to the assistance we received from Mr. Zupljanin and Mr. Brano Buhovac, who was first head of the forensic centre, that we were able to set up our forensic centre in Banja Luka, and then, in the beginning of 1993, we managed to locate some quality people who we hired for that work and sent them for training. And we also moved some workers of the Banja Luka forensic department to the Banja Luka CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to focus on the first part of your answer and would seek some clarifications from you. In the first sentence of your answer, you told us what the duties of the members of the interior are, once they learn that a crime was committed. Tell us, please, these operative steps that are taken, the ones that you enumerated, are these steps taken based on their duty, as regulated by law, or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These steps are taken pursuant to their duties regulated by the Law on Criminal Proceedings, and the Law on the Ministry of the Interior -- the Law on Internal Affairs. Once they collect information from the sites where the crime was committed, if the perpetrators are unknown, then a criminal complaint is filed against an unknown perpetrator. And in that complaint, they have to list the facts and also they have to list any attachments. When it comes to serious crimes, homicide, violent crimes, and so on, typically investigative judge has to come to the on-site investigation. When it comes to property crimes, they were not duty-bound to go to the on-site investigation. Rather, they authorised members of the Ministry of the Interior to carry that out. These are typical, routine procedures in place when there is a functioning system.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand all that. You explained about the situation in 1992. I want to know about the following: Information is received suggesting that a crime was committed in an area covered by a certain SJB. Is it necessary for you, as head of the crime prevention administration at the HQ, to order an investigation, to order this SJB and its members to start an investigation to collect operative intelligence, evidence, information, or is that not necessary?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Law on Internal Affairs and the Law on Criminal Procedure are very specific about this, about the respective jurisdictions. When a crime is committed and information reaches the SJB and its members, by default, they start taking action from their own purview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So they have a responsibility to, by default, as you say, take measures. Is that part of their duties under the law?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So, in order to launch an investigation like this, in order to set in motion the operative procedures by members of the police, your answer, at page 43, line 20, I think, was that you were not required to issue a specific order in that respect. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Based on Mr. Hannis's comment which I described as the reason for this line of questions, was the minister's order required to launch an investigation like that and take operative measures like that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No order of the minister was required.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, you spoke about forensic examinations a minute ago carried out in 1992, and you also talked about the problems that you encountered. You spoke about the Banja Luka CSB, saying that, back in 1992, they partially carried out such examinations because, if my understanding is correct, this was the only centre that was appropriately equipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 430D1. Tab 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a memo, or letter, dated the 23rd of September, 1992, produced by the Banja Luka CSB. There's a cover letter, saying that the findings of the forensic analysis in connection with the killing of Dzevamira Remic is being delivered to the SJB here, as well as the wounding of Husein Ramic, who was slightly wounded, and Selim Cajic, who was seriously wounded, which occurred on the 9th of September, 1992, signed here by Milorad Djuric, described here as chief of department. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what sort of the duty he discharged back in 1992? Which institution did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an employee of the Banja Luka CSB. He was head of a department there. This document itself, I started discussing that a while ago -- some of the forensic work in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina for the purposes of public security stations was conducted by the forensic technicians of the CSB. In more complex cases, where a more complex forensic analysis was required, this was done by the Ministry of the Interior because the equipment was there. This is an example where a ballistic report was produced for the purposes of a public security station. What we see them doing here is delivering their finds but in this specific case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you prompted us now with a hint now in terms of the forensic work. Let's go back to 1992. At the time, was there an institution, a centre, within the MUP that had the capacity to perform such complex forensic work in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no such centre or institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 3 of this document, we see a signature. It appears to be the signature of the person who carried out the examination; the forensic expert, in other words. It reads: "Vilko Maric, machine engineer, inspector with the Banja Luka CSB." Are you familiar with this person, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Vilko Maric was an employee of the forensic department of the Banja Luka CSB. He was an expert for ballistics, specifically. And when the centre was established within the crime prevention service in Banja Luka, he was seconded by the centre to the forensic centre. He became head of the crime prevention department there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the last page of this document, sir. We have the original memo containing the request of the Sipovo SJB concerning this forensic examination. The date there is the 11th of September, 1992, signed by chief of the SJB, Jovo Bogdanovic. Is Mr. Bogdanovic familiar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know his last name, but I didn't know the man. The document itself that you're showing me is a procedural way for a station to address the public security station with a request for an examination and a short description to be provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D653, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next document: 420D1, tab 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, another document by the Ministry of the Interior, specifically the Banja Luka CSB, dated the 27th of August, 1992. Typewritten, department chief, Milorad Djuric. The document being sent to military post 4627, military police. Subject: Forensic report on fire-arms in relation to the murder of Culum Camo, Sefik, Nijaz, Amir, and Selim, which occurred on the 15th of August, 1992, in Bastasi village, Banja Luka municipality. Sir, do you know that the Banja Luka CSB carried out any forensic examinations in 1992 in response to requests made by military bodies, bodies of military security, more specifically.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew about that. It wasn't just in 1992. It was later on, as well, when the forensic centre was set up within the administration. Military police didn't have their own forensic institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Last page, page 4, we see a letter there by the Banja Luka military police. The date is the 23rd of August, 1992. They are sending an automatic rifle and a machine-gun to be forensically examined. These having previously been seized from people named Radenko Sugic and Obrenko Sugic. You see that, don't you? It was signed by Lieutenant Ostoja Trifunovic on behalf of the commander.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the established procedure. The public security station forwards a case, the case file. This has to be followed by a request explaining what is expected. So these are the weapons in question here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm looking at the first and last names of the victims involved in this incident that occurred on the 15th of August in Bastasi village, Banja Luka municipality. Are you able to tell the ethnicity of these victims, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
