utterances.text: And what about the weapons that were temporarily seized from these three persons, Miladen, Radenko, and Obrenko Sugic? Can you tell their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miladen, Radenko, and Obrenko are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At page 3, we see a signature on the expert report. Again, Vilko Maric. You agree, sir, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I move that this be admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I guess I'm not sure what the relevance of this particular one is to show that forensic works were being done. If it is about this particular murder and the case against the Sugic brothers, that is a very long and complicated story. And this document standing by itself would be rather misleading. So depending on specifically what purpose it is for, I may not have an objection. If I could have some elaboration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe the case file of Sugic brothers was -- is already an exhibit in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that case, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D654, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness please be shown 336D1, tab 74.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: While that is coming up, Your Honour, could I request that that be sent for revision of the translation because it doesn't capture the diacritics correctly, as far as the names of the family. My English translation has a bracket as the first letter in the Cula family name, and I think it is important to have the names correct. And Mr. Djuric, who is the department chief, is a /URI bracket.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you're referring to document 1D654, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, tab 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was just notified that the document that we re-uploaded in the e-court with the Serbian diacritics. The original diacritics --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this is a document of the first-instance court in Kljuc dated the 5th of October 1992; the lower court in Kljuc. Report of an on-site investigation. A crime which took place on the 4th of October, 1992, in the settlement of Pudin Han where two dead bodies were found. Sir -- three dead bodies, actually. I apologise. Dedic, Hatidza; Draganovic, Latif; and Draganovic, Selva. Are you familiar with this case, Mr. Macar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not this specific case, but I'm familiar with some of the people who were involved in the on-site investigation. One of the previous questions you asked me, I explained the procedure applied by the SJBs and centres, what they did as soon as they learned that a crime was committed. So this is a case of violent crimes, crimes against life and limb, the investigating magistrate is informed. He goes to the scene and he runs the on-site investigation. People from the forensics unit and other policemen are there. I knew the inspector, Mr. Todo Gajic. I also remember Mr. Gojko who was the forensic technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Bade on the names of the victims here, Hatidza Dedic, Latif Draganovic and Selva Draganovic, what seems to be their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The victims are clearly Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have three on-site investigation records like this. They are all relevant in relation to the indictment since they're all in reference to 1992. The following document is tab 76, 337D1. That, too, is in relation to incidents referred to in the indictment in this trial. I move, therefore, that this document be admitted. It might be used to show what an on-site investigation report or record looks like. And the same goes for the remaining two documents that are very much like this one. But I do not wish to waste the Chamber's time since the documents are very similar, both in terms of substance and in terms of shape, only in reference to other crimes and other specific incidents. In each of these documents that it is my intention to tender, we find references to Muslim victims. This is one of the key issues raised in this case. For that reason, I would like to ask the Chamber to instruct me. What course of action are we to take on this? Shall we take the established approach and show one of these documents, just to explain, and then simply tender the remaining two without necessarily producing them in open court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I would think so. But could you assist me, Mr. Zecevic, by explaining what you mean, as appears at line 8 and 9 of page 50, that: "In relation to incidents referred to in the indictment in this trial."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I believe the incident in Pudin Han, in the village of Pudin Han, is the incident in the indictment. I can give the reference. I don't have it right ready at this point, but I am very sure that both Pudin Han and the victim of Kamicak, which are in the municipality Kljuc, are the specific incidents in our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to make a request that since it appears that this witness isn't really in a position to assist us very much about these specific documents other than the general nature of them reflecting the record of an on-site investigation, that Mr. Zecevic offer these documents in writing through a bar table motion. Because I don't feel prepared here standing on my feet now looking at tab 76 and being able to tell you whether or not it relates to an incident in the indictment, et cetera. And I would prefer to have the opportunity to deal with it that way, because I'm not going to be able to do anything with this witness about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, what about marking them for identification, pending the verification [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no problem with that. Then I feel I would have an opportunity to deal with it. Thank you. That's a good idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zecevic, that's the course we will follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. May I reed the numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And the tab numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The first document is 65 ter 336D1, tab number 74; the second document is 337D1, tab 76; and the last document is 349D1, tab 67.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, they will become Exhibits 1D655, 1D656, and 1D657, all marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I should like this criminal complaint to be shown to the witness, which is document 341D1, the tab being 97.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a criminal report dated the 4th of December, 1992, filed by Mr. Savo Tepic, chief of the Kotor Varos public security station, filed with the public prosecutor's office in Kotor Varos. The criminal report was filed against -- because of a murder which took place on the 18th of August, 1992, to the detriment of Niko Orsulic and Mara Orsulic, from the village of Cepak, Kotor Varos municipality. Do you know this person, Savo Tepic, the chief of the public security station?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us on the basis of the names, names of the victims here, of the injured parties here, can you tell us what is their -- what their ethnicity is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The victims are of Croat ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of this investigation that was conducted by the Kotor Varos public security station and the public prosecutor's office in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with the actual criminal report -- not of the actual criminal report itself, but I believe that the report that we subsequently got from the public security station, there were references and information regarding this incident as well. This is a classical example of communication between a public security station and the public prosecutor's office where, in relation of a certain incident with an unknown perpetrator, criminal reports would be submitted with supporting material to the office. In the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there were prescribed forms which were the starting point for filing criminal complaints against unknown perpetrators, and so on. Namely, it was only towards the end of 1992 and 1993 that we managed to obtain some material for the public security stations and the public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm particularly interested in your comment on the last page of this document. That is, a letter of the public prosecutor's office sent to the public security station in connection with this criminal report on the 22nd of December, 1992. This is signed by the public prosecutor Zoran Zubic, or Bubic, I'm not sure. In paragraph 2 of this letter, it is stated: "You need to find and establish the perpetrator of the crime." And: "Should you detect him, collect all necessary information." And so on and so forth: "Please submit them to our above number together with a report." Tell me, Mr. Macar, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is routine correspondence between the competent public prosecutor and the organ of the interior upon receiving a criminal complaint involving an unknown perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me whether it was in this way that the public prosecutor's office issued instructions to the public security station to take specific measures in connection with a criminal complaint received?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would issue them instructions to take operative action upon receiving the criminal complaint in order to detect the perpetrator, as well as the actions that normally follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Explain this -- what is written in the last sentence: "The statute of limitation for the above crime is August 2017."

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In practice, it was very infrequent by prosecutors to indicate the statute of limitations period because this was something which is normally known under the law. But this obviously was a diligent prosecutor. Of course, the organs of the interior knew in the particular instance what -- when the period would lapse under the statute of limitations. In the pre-war period, I occasion to see prosecutors acting in a similar fashion in Sarajevo. It was not customary practice, but when I worked as an inspector prior to the war, I had occasion to see this also.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it your recollection also that the statute of limitations applicable to prosecution for the crime of murder or qualified murder was 25 years?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, off the top of my head, I believe that this -- there -- this didn't fall under the statute of limitations at all, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I should like to tendered this document as well. It is relevant and it is related to the municipality of Kotor Varos, which features in our indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I do have an objection because I'm not completely convinced about the relevance, the fact that it occurred in Kotor Varos and the victims apparently had names of Croats. But as far as the perpetrator, all we have is, in this document, some information that he appeared to be a reservist and he said his name was Boris, the same as the four-year-old child whose parents were killed. But I note on the first page the criminal report says on-site investigation was not carried out because the site of the crime was under paramilitary control. And in the second page of the English on the Official Note of interview, at the bottom it says: "Since the house was located in the enemy controlled area, it's impossible to carry out an on-site investigation." This leads me to believe that the perpetrator may not have been a Serb at all but may have been a Croat or a Muslim military man. So I don't see how that is relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I do agree that it might be anybody because the unknown perpetrator is -- but I believe I understood the point of the Prosecutor's case was that the crimes against non-Serbs were treated in a discriminatory matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It has been our position that the crimes against non-Serbs commit by Serbs are at the heart of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, with all due --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Crimes against non-Serbs committed by other non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But with all due respect, Your Honours, it is unknown perpetrated [sic]. It can be a Serb. I agree, it can be somebody else. Even the persons who were conducting and filing this criminal report didn't know whether it was a Serb or any other -- other nationality of the perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D658.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we take the break and come back in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, the -- we understand that you are unlikely to finished within 15 minutes. And in the circumstances, we propose to take the adjournment now, when the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. I was already advised by the Registrar. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked for a few minutes. I need to raise a procedural issue. Namely -- or shall that be done after this witness -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. Because the Chamber itself has a rule to go give.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can do that on Monday, Your Honour, if I may. Concerning agreements about adjudicated facts or adjudication about agreed facts, on Monday, if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, we have had you brought back -- escorted back into the courtroom in order to formally release you for the weekend. It is obvious that we are unable to complete your examination-in-chief today, and therefore, the Chamber has certain procedural matters with which to deal before it rises. But we would now excuse you to return when the Chamber resumes on Monday morning. And this being a lengthy break, I remind you of the cautions I gave you earlier about not discussing the case with anyone outside of the courtroom, and, of course, you can have no contact with counsel. And we trust that you have a weekend to recover and to be with us again on Monday morning. Was there something you wish -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just out of an abundance of caution, Mr. Krgovic, in order to save time for his cross-examination, asked the usher to give the witness three documents, rather lengthy documents that he intends to ask the witness about. I agree that is a good time-saving measure, and I support it. But I would ask that it be made clear to the witness the prohibition about discussing the case with anybody includes talking about the documents he's been given to read. I had a witness one time who saw a distinction between talking about his testimony and talking about documents that he was reading. So that's why I asked that we make that clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Macar, I don't know that I need to repeat what you would have just heard Mr. Hannis said, but did you understand Mr. Hannis's comment? Do I need to add anything further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did understand. I understand what you said, Your Honour, and I understood Mr. Hannis's comment. I have received a document, and I'm perfectly aware of with whom I should not be in contact. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So the usher would now escort you from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has the following oral ruling: On the 2nd of May, 2011, the Trial Chamber accepted Mladen Bajagic as an expert for the Defence of Mico Stanisic and deferred its decision on the admission of his report and related documents till the conclusion of his testimony. Mladen Bajagic testified from the 2nd to the 10th of May, 2011. On the 10th of May, upon the conclusion of the expert's testimony, the Defence withdrew Annexes 1 to 11 of his report, in view of the fact that those documents had been retyped and were not authored by Mr. Bajagic. The Stanisic Defence requested the admission of the report and related documents, including an updated curriculum vitae, and indicated that the Defence would provide a list of footnoted documents to be admitted along with the report. The Prosecution reiterated its objection to the admission of the report in its entirety. It sought and was granted permission to file a written submission limited to addressing the footnoted document. The list was provided to the Prosecution by e-mail on 16 May 2011. On the 18th of May, the Prosecution filed a motion objecting to 19 of the 59 footnoted documents on the basis that they are either irrelevant, present a tu quoque defence, or that their provenance is unknown. The Defence submits that the 19 footnoted documents do not present a tu quoque defence, since it is entirely legitimate to place events in a social, historical, political, and military context, particularly in view of the fact that Mr. Bajagic used a multi-disciplinary approach in analysing and discussing issues relevant to the RS MUP. The Defence also addressed the challenge to provenance in relation to two documents. The Trial Chamber notes that the Prosecution challenged Mr. Bajagic's report in its entirety, inter alia, due to the "his questionable methodology and source documents." In the alternative, the Prosecution objected to the admission of several sections of the report, on the basis that they are tu quoque in nature, irrelevant and beyond the scope of the witness's expertise. The Trial Chamber finds that indeed several passages referred to by the Prosecution are not particularly relevant to the case. However, the Trial Chamber finds that these passages refer to the background of the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina and are important to understand the report as a whole. Trial Chamber finds that the Bajagic -- that the Bajagic's report is generally relevant. The Trial Chamber findings that although a number of the footnoted documents may appear to lack relevance when considered in isolation, they are relevant to the expert's conclusions and opinions on matters discussed in the report. Consequently, they constitute inseparable parts of the report without which the Chamber is not able to fully understand and assess the issues discussed in the body of the report. It will be a matter for the Trial Chamber at an appropriate time to determine the weight to be given to the report and related documents, in light of the Trial Chamber record as a whole. The report, its Annex 12, and all 59 footnoted documents tendered by the Defence, and Mr. Bajagic's updated CV, are, therefore, admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to raise an issue. I've already spoken to Mr. Hannis about it. While preparing our Defence and during the production of our 65 ter list, both that of the Stanisic Defence than of the Zupljanin Defence, the two Defence teams have co-ordinated our work, in order to avoid any documents appearing on both lists, or any duplication of evidence. Some of the Zupljanin relevant documents are on the 65 ter Stanisic list, although they're actually in reference to the Zupljanin indictment. Therefore, I wanted to submit a motion to be allowed to use Mr. Stanisic' 65 ter document in my own case since some of these are, so to speak, documents shared and evidence shared by both teams, some of these appearing on Mr. Stanisic's list and not on our list for purely technical reasons in order to avoid duplication, as I have already explained. That is all from me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, do you have any comment on what appears to be an eminently sensible and practical suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I really don't have a problem with that. I assume that we will get the usual notice before a witness testifies, and they will list documents and whether it has a P number or a 1D number, or a 2D number. That doesn't seem to matter to me. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we grant the motion, as prayed. And, Mr. Hannis, you said you would come back to us on Monday with the matters that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment until Monday. Everyone would have seen that next week is staggered, both in terms of courtrooms and times, so persons would be forgiven if they make the mistake that I made this morning of turning up in two wrong courtrooms, but we'll see where we go. So consult the schedule, and we reconvene on Monday morning. And I trust everybody has a safe weekend.
